newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM advises exiled prince against return.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM advises exiled prince against return.

text.p: Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Wednesday he had advised his uncle, exiled prince Norodom Sirivudh, to postpone plans to return home.

Ranariddh said he hoped Sirivudh, who left for exile in France in December 1995 after being detained for alleged involvement in a plot to assassinate Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, would not go ahead with plans to return to Phnom Penh next week.

"I hope he will not come back as planned on the 14th (April)...I have advised him personally not to come back yet," Ranariddh said of Sirivudh, who is the half-brother of the premier's father King Norodom Sihanouk.
"You have seen the king's response," Ranariddh told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

He was referring to Sihanouk's April 7 letter to Ranariddh, in which he threatened to resign immediately if the Sirivudh affair led to violence between Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP), which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
"There will not be any resorting to force," said the prince.
Tensions between the two leading parties reached boiling point after a deadly grenade attack on a demonstration on March 30 led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.
Sihanouk, whose intervention allowed Sirivudh to leave for France in December 1995, also said he was in no position to make an enemy of Hun Sen by granting an amnesty.
Sirivudh, who denies allegations of plotting against Hun Sen, was sentenced to 10 years' jail in absentia in a trial the international community branded a travesty.
Ranariddh recently urged the king to grant amnesty to Sirivudh, but Hun Sen has refused to support a pardon.

Sihanouk, who sparked a fresh political crisis in February by saying he was unhappy on the throne and was thinking of quitting, told his son Ranariddh it was up to FUNCINPEC and the CPP to resolve the Sirivudh case in the interests of the country.
